clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man with remote Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (35 years prior) presented with 8 months of severe steatorrhea (10-15 oily/greasy stools daily, foul-smelling gas), profound malabsorption (41-kg weight loss despite high caloric intake), and complications of malnutrition (progressive muscle weakness, recurrent falls). Diagnostic workup confirmed severe EPI with fecal elastase <40 μg/g and massive steatorrhea (277g fat/24h). CT enterography demonstrated marked pancreatic atrophy without malignancy, establishing the structural basis for EPI in the context of prior bariatric surgery. Laboratory studies confirmed consequences of malabsorption including severe fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (25-hydroxyvitamin D 9.4 ng/mL, vitamin A 15.8 mcg/dL, vitamin E 4.7 mcg/dL), hypoalbuminemia (2.8 g/dL), and hypocalcemia (7.9 mg/dL). Treatment with pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) 2 tablets TID resulted in resolution of diarrhea and weight regain to baseline within 2 months, confirming the diagnosis.
